author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces accept an optional specialty and then list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching uses the whole specialty name and disregards letter case. A blank value behaves as an absent one, and a specialty no veterinarian holds is answered normally with an empty list.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable document is requested, then it carries each veterinarian and their specialties.
Given a named specialty, when the directory page is opened, then only the veterinarians holding it are listed, a page at a time.
Given a named specialty, when the machine-readable document is requested, then it carries only the veterinarians holding it.
Given a specialty named in a different letter case, when either surface is requested, then it matches the same veterinarians.
Given text that only begins a specialty's name, when either surface is requested, then it matches no veterinarian.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is requested, then the request succeeds and the list is empty.
Given a specialty that is blank or only spaces, when either surface is requested, then the result matches a request naming none.
Given no specialty named, when either surface is requested, then every veterinarian is listed.
Given a narrowed list spanning more than one page, when a paging link is followed, then the next page stays narrowed to the same specialty.
non_goals: No form, dropdown, or other page control on either surface
Free-text veterinarian search, which NG-9 still declines
Filtering the directory by any attribute other than specialty
notes: Owner decision: the filter is named on the request only, as an optional parameter named specialty on both surfaces, and pagination links carry it so a narrowed page stays navigable. Route and parameter spelling belong in system-design.md#contracts, which also needs the VetController and VetRepository rows to cite REQ-VET-003. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused; the machine-readable surface returns under REQ-VET-003. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-12-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md — that file is owned by system-design-expert, outside this agent's write scope. Open question recorded in the PRD: whether the directory later carries a visible specialty control.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Narrow non-goal NG-9. Free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope; filtering the directory by an attribute it already displays (specialty) is in scope. Record the narrowing the way this project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter extends the existing feature-package shape rather than adding structure: two derived reads on VetRepository, an optional request parameter on both VetController handlers, and the specialty threaded through the vetList paging links. No service layer, no new package, no schema or seed change. Two decisions are fresh ground and are now recorded: case is folded in the query rather than in the column collation, and the filtered reads are not cached (system-design.md#veterinarian-directory-reads, adr/2026-08-12-uncached-filtered-vet-reads.md). Resolution basis is grep over the vet package plus OwnerController and OwnerRepository; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetRepository gains one paged and one collection read narrowed by specialty name, matching the whole name and folding case; neither carries a caching annotation

VetController's two handlers take an optional specialty; a blank or whitespace value normalizes to absent and selects the existing unfiltered read, so today's behavior is untouched when the parameter is missing
vetList.html paging links carry the specialty; the controller adds it to the model for the template to read
Vet, Specialty, the vendor schemas, and the seed data are unchanged — matching uses the existing vet_specialties join and the eager many-to-many already mapped on Vet

patterns.description: derived query returning a Page for a Pageable — the shape the filtered paged read follows, with case folding expressed in the derivation rather than left to the column

blank-or-absent request text normalized before the repository call. Reuse the normalization only; the not-found rejection that follows it does not apply, since an unmatched specialty answers with an empty list
the existing pagination helper and its page-size local; the filtered read plugs in here rather than beside it

risks.risk: The vets cache region is declared with statistics only — no size bound and no eviction. A cached read keyed by caller-supplied text lets any caller mint unbounded entries.
risks.mitigation: The filtered reads carry no caching annotation; the unfiltered reads keep theirs. Recorded in adr/2026-08-12-uncached-filtered-vet-reads.md.

risks.risk: The existing paging links build URLs with Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__), which inlines the value into the link expression before it is evaluated. Safe for the integer page number, unsafe for caller-supplied text.
risks.mitigation: Carry the specialty as a link parameter — the @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=...)} form — so the value is URL-encoded and never becomes expression source. Do not extend the preprocessing form to it.

risks.risk: The owner list template drops its filter from the paging links. Copying that template loses the specialty on page two.
risks.mitigation: theFilteredVetListShouldKeepTheSpecialtyWhenPaging asserts the rendered link carries the specialty.

risks.risk: Relying on column collation for case-insensitive matching would repeat the PostgreSQL owner-search defect, where the same request answers differently per vendor.
risks.mitigation: Fold case in the query. The behavior then holds identically on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, and the H2-backed suite is representative.

risks.risk: Whole-name matching drifts to a prefix or substring derivation, admitting the free-text search NG-9 still declines.
risks.mitigation: The finder derivation ends at equality on the specialty name; theSpecialtyFilterShouldRequireTheWholeSpecialtyName pins it.

risks.risk: Paging a query that joins an eagerly-fetched many-to-many can report a total that disagrees with the page content.
risks.mitigation: The join table holds each veterinarian-specialty pair once, so the join yields no duplicate rows. The paging test asserts the page total alongside the listed veterinarians.

notes: Autofix audit: the log carries no design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to audit. Durable-memory writes made under this verdict: docs/adr/2026-08-12-uncached-filtered-vet-reads.md (new); docs/adr/README.md index rows for that ADR and for the non-goal ADR the PRD author could not index; system-design.md Contracts rows for VetController and VetRepository now cite REQ-VET-003, and the Vets row moves from an em-dash to REQ-VET-003, which makes the section's 'three kinds' sentence accurate again; a new 'Veterinarian directory reads' subsection; the Known Defects row saying the machine-readable route serves no requirement is retired, as the non-goal ADR's Consequences state; Open Question 5 narrowed to the unfiltered reads. On the PRD author's request to record route and parameter spelling in Contracts: the section's own standing rule forbids transcribing parameters, since source is authoritative. The filter's shape is recorded in prose instead of a route table — surfacing the tension rather than overriding either side. On architecture-principles' bar that no new business rule enters a controller: normalizing blank to absent and choosing between the filtered and unfiltered read is request binding and response selection, both admitted by the Web controller row. The matching rule itself lives in the repository derivation. Observation outside this slice: the owner list paging links do not carry lastName, so page two of a narrowed owner search widens back to every owner. Not settled here — it needs the PRD owner, and REQ-OWN-002 and REQ-OWN-004 are untouched by this slice.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived query findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String[, Pageable]) in VetRepository.java; no string-concatenated query text, no @Query, no EntityManager call is introduced, so the value is bound as a parameter (security-principles.md 'Injection into data access').

XSS: mitigation 2 verified in templates/vets/vetList.html. All six paging links use the link-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}; no __${...}__ preprocessing survives in that template, so caller text is URL-encoded by Thymeleaf and attribute-escaped rather than becoming link-expression source. Swept the whole templates/ tree for th:utext and __${: no th:utext anywhere, and every remaining __${...}__ occurrence is pre-existing and fed by entity ids, fragment names, or ints, none by this change.

Cache poisoning / unbounded-key vector: mitigation 1 verified in VetRepository.java. @Cacheable("vets") appears only on the two pre-existing unfiltered findAll methods (lines 45 and 55); both new filtered reads carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no caching annotation, so caller text never enters a key of the size-unbounded, eviction-free vets region configured in system/CacheConfiguration.java.

Reflected output: the specialty is not echoed into the page body or into the /vets JSON; it appears only inside th:href link parameters and in the th:with narrowed guard. The href base is a literal path, so no javascript:/scheme injection is reachable.

Boundary handling: namedSpecialty() in VetController.java normalizes null/blank to null before the value crosses into data access, and both surfaces share that one normalization, so the two routes cannot diverge on what counts as no filter.

Exposed surface: no new endpoint. Two existing read-only GET routes gain one optional query parameter; no mutating path, no binder, and no actuator exposure is touched, so the change does not widen the baseline in system-design.md Security Context.

Supply chain: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only shows no build.gradle, settings.gradle, or gradle.properties change and no new import of a third-party library, so no dependency is added or upgraded and no NVD check is implicated.

Secrets: swept the diff for credential-shaped additions (token, password, secret, key, credential, datasource URL). The only added string literals are specialty names and test fixtures; no new credential, connection string, or committed default appears.

author: change-grader
summary: filter the vet directory by specialty on both surfaces

blast_radius.note: Eleven files but one module: the vet feature package (VetController, VetRepository), its own vetList template, two test classes, and six documentation files. No schema, seed data, build file, dependency, or security-sensitive path is touched, and the extractor reports no sensitive paths; the 43 hunks are mostly the six paging links rewritten one at a time plus doc and ADR prose, not reach into unrelated code.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk and found no behavior the description would not predict. The unfiltered paths are untouched (findPaginated and the JSON handler both fall through to the original cached findAll when the normalized specialty is null), namedSpecialty strips and maps empty to null once for both surfaces so they cannot diverge, the derived query parameterizes the caller text rather than concatenating it, the filtered reads deliberately carry no cache annotation so request text never keys the unbounded vets region, and every rewritten paging link uses the Thymeleaf link-parameter form so the value is URL-encoded rather than spliced into the expression. The one non-obvious risk in this shape, paging a query that joins the eager vet_specialties many-to-many where a wrong count or in-memory pagination would be invisible under a mock, is pinned by a real H2 test asserting a total of 2 with a page of 1.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes and each would fail against a plausible broken implementation: dropping the case fold fails shouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialtyNamedInAnotherCase, a prefix match fails shouldNotFindVetsFromTextThatOnlyBeginsASpecialtyName, losing the blank normalization fails theBlankSpecialtyShouldListEveryVet on both surfaces, and dropping the specialty from a paging link fails theFilteredVetListShouldKeepTheSpecialtyWhenPaging. The split is sound: query semantics against real H2 in ClinicServiceTests, the URL contract through MockMvc, plus a regression pin that unfiltered paging links still render as before and an encoding test using a value carrying URL syntax. The empty-result HTML case asserts the empty listVets model attribute positively rather than a vacuous absence-of-names check.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched roster reviewers, the full battery the high-risk review plan called for, approved in round two with zero findings, no escalate tag, and no lingering caveat in their approved aspects. Round one carried two fixable test-only findings from the test-reviewer; the implementer fixed both with a stronger assertion than proposed and the test-reviewer explicitly accepted the substitutions as improvements.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, no design revision (two design-block records exist but both are verdict new and the second only extends supporting_paths with the ADR files, so the row's 0 is right). The diff stays inside the design-block's primary and supporting paths, and the one boundary move that would otherwise look like drift, narrowing non-goal NG-9 and reviving the machine-readable surface under a fresh id, is carried by a recorded scope_overrides owner decision in the PRD entry and by a non-goal ADR, with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn. The declared non-goal of no page control holds: no form or dropdown appears in the template.

rationale: Every production hunk read: the unfiltered paths keep their exact prior behavior, blank normalization is shared by both surfaces, the query is parameterized and uncached by design, and the paging links URL-encode. Confirm and merge; if you read one thing first, read the two new ADRs, since they move a product boundary.
